Answers to the open items of this request, with files (all committed in `world/experiment-repo` `main`, commit 4977245 and later; one correction at the end that changes wording you already have).
  > 
  > **Where things are**
  > - Secondary endpoint n/N = 2 %: `results/twopct/` (`primary.csv`, `primary_suite.csv`, `selected.csv`, `per_bench`, `ratio_by_n`, …); n is labelled `0` there, the real budget is `round(0.02·N)` (column `n_actual` in `per_bench`/`targets`). Three main splits only (interp, lineage, extrap); extrap10/extrap50 are not run at 2 %.
  > - LOBO-selected class representatives (chosen without the held-out benchmark): `results/selected.csv`, `results/twopct/selected.csv`; suites all/OLL/HELM in `primary_suite.csv`. Columns `split, cls, held_out, suite, baseline, chosen, ratio, ci_lo, ci_hi, n_bench` (rows with `held_out` empty are the pooled geometric means; the row with "k distinct, mode …" gives the number of different choices over the held-out benchmarks).
  > - Larger-gap nested split: `results/inner50/` (same schema as the main results).
  > - Source count: `results/msrc.csv` (M = 0 means all sources).
  > - Per-target bias: `bias2_unbiased` and `n_draws` columns of `per_bench.csv.gz` (n = 100). The high-R run (R = 100 at n = 100 for the non-adaptive designs) is queued; I report when it is analysed and until then the bias² column is the R = 10/40 one, corrected for the MC variance of the mean.
  > - Stronger anchor k-means (n_init 10, max_iter 300): `results/kmstrong.csv`.
  > 
  > **Results to take over** (RMSE ratio to `uniform|mean`, geometric mean over non-thin benchmarks; representative of each class chosen leave-one-benchmark-out, rows `held_out = ALL`; in brackets the same class with the representative chosen on all 13 benchmarks, `held_out = POSTHOC`, where it differs)
  > 
  > | class | n=100 interp | lineage | extrap | extrap10 | extrap50 | 2 % interp | lineage | extrap |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  > | design-based (mean, calreg) | 0.71 | 0.73 | 0.77 | 0.76 | 0.83 | 0.58 | 0.60 | 0.78 [0.75] |
  > | difference-corrected | 0.65 | 0.73 [0.70] | 0.87 [0.84,0.89] ([0.82]) | 0.74 [0.70] | 1.01 [0.95] | 0.54 | 0.57 | 0.78 [0.73] |
  > | model-based | 0.65 | 0.69 | 0.84 | 0.75 | 1.21 | 0.54 | 0.56 | 0.83 |
  > | anchor | 0.72 | 0.79 | 1.01 | 1.00 | 1.34 | 0.51 | 0.54 | 0.81 |
  > | info/adaptive (cat) | 0.68 | 0.67 | 1.04 | 0.99 | 1.67 [1.47] | 0.51 | 0.51 | 0.74 [0.71] |
  > 
  > Ratios to `strat|mean` (second baseline), same rows: n = 100 extrap difference-corrected 1.03 selected [0.96 post hoc], design-based 0.91, model-based 1.00; extrap10 0.88 [0.84] / 0.91 / 0.90; extrap50 1.14 [1.07] / 0.95 / 1.37; interp 0.80 / 0.88 / 0.80; lineage 0.88 [0.84] / 0.88 / 0.83. At 2 % extrap: difference-corrected 0.93 [0.87], design-based 0.92 [0.90], model-based 0.99, anchor 0.96, cat 0.88 [0.85]. Intervals (95 % family bootstrap) are in the files; those of the POSTHOC rows are optimistic.
  > 
  > Reading: in extrapolation at n = 100 the best method chosen without the held-out benchmark does not beat stratified sampling by difference correction (1.03); what survives selection is the design-based `balanced|calreg` (0.77 vs uniform, 0.91 vs strat). The extrap gain over stratified sampling is scale-dependent (at 2 % the LOBO-selected classes are 0.88–0.96 of strat, model-based 0.99). In interp and lineage at n = 100 every class is below strat (0.80–0.89 interp, 0.80–0.94 lineage).
  > 
  > **Validity points you should carry**
  > 1. The post-hoc best of ~100 methods is better than the leave-one-benchmark-out one (difference-corrected extrap 0.82 vs 0.87; extrap50 0.95 vs 1.01). The paper must say which is which.
  > 2. "Model-based loses" holds for the pure IRT predictors (`irt-model`/`irt-plugin`), not for the class: `balanced|ridge-plugin` is 0.84 vs uniform in extrap (1.00 vs strat); at extrap50 the class does lose (1.21).
